newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMANY'S DAX, BOOSTED BY DOLLAR, UP ABOUT ONE PCT.
newsitem.headline: GERMANY'S DAX, BOOSTED BY DOLLAR, UP ABOUT ONE PCT.

text.p: Germany's DAX index rose about one percent in pre-bourse dealings on Thursday, getting a lift from overnight Wall Street gains and the dollar edging toward 1.89 marks in European activity.
Dealers said the German share market had a positive undertone and looked for further gains during the session despite modest losses in the German debt market.
But dealers also noted that volumes were relatively thin in many DAX component shares in IBIS computer dealings and said gains may be capped unless investor interest picks up.

Market focus remained on banking shares as Deutsche Bank AG was among the top volume shares, rising 1.35 marks to 119 marks, amid ongoing speculation about further banking industry mergers or takeovers.
Commerzbank AG, considered a top takeover target, was up 23 pfennigs at 62.70 marks, while Dresdner Bank AG was up 89 marks at 79.50 marks.

Utility Veba AG gained 1.70 marks to 113 marks after reporting a rise in first-half net profit to 816 million marks from 743 million marks behind a rise in sales to 39.7 billion marks from 36.6 billion marks in the 1996 period.
Sportswear group Adidas AG surged 4.70 marks to 227 marks after reporting results on Wednesday.
Paribas Capital Markets raised Adidas to buy from no action, citing the outlook for Adidas to keep up high double-digit gains in sales and operating profit for 1997.
Chemicals group Henkel was also a strong performer, rising 4.75 marks to 107.10 marks on market rumours that the share was upgraded by a U.S. investment house.
